sheet.summary: Local tradition recounts that a black basalt monolith washed ashore along the Panasnala River centuries ago, and Lord Shani appeared in a dream promising complete protection against theft on condition that the slab remained under the open sky and villagers discarded doors. Archaeological excavations across the surrounding Nevasa basin by Deccan College established extensive prehistoric and early historic occupational horizons, while physical surveys at Shani Shingnapur document an open-air basalt stele alongside modern commercial institutions adapted with concealed security measures. Sociologists and anti-superstition organizations contend that the village's zero-crime claim is a heavily commercialized myth contradicted by police first information reports and hidden electromagnetic locks, whereas traditional residents maintain that faith and fear of karmic retribution effectively deter wrongdoing. It remains historically unverified when the practice of doorless dwellings first began in the village and whether the central monolith originated as a pre-historic aniconic megalith before its integration into regional Shani worship.
